Bed Bugs

Best Bed Bug Treatment: What Actually Works in 2024

By Shaw's Pest Control  ·  Wichita, KS

What Is the Best Bed Bug Treatment That Actually Works?

If you're researching the best bed bug treatment, you've likely already confirmed you have an infestation—and you want it gone fast. Bed bugs are notoriously difficult to eliminate because they hide in cracks, seams, and voids where sprays can't reach. In Wichita and across Kansas, we've treated hundreds of infestations since 1987, and we've learned one thing: not all treatments are equal. Some methods require multiple visits and still leave survivors. Others eliminate the problem in a single day. This post breaks down the four main treatment methods—heat, chemical, steam, and DIY—so you understand what works, what doesn't, and why. We hold three State Certifications and a Master Tech Certification, and we'll give you the straight answer: the best bed bug treatment depends on your timeline, budget, and how thorough you need the results to be.

Why Heat Treatment Is the Most Effective Bed Bug Solution

Heat treatment is the gold standard for bed bug elimination because it's the only method proven to kill all life stages—eggs, nymphs, and adults—in one visit. Bed bugs die when exposed to temperatures of 118°F for 90 minutes or 122°F for just a few minutes. Professional heat treatments raise the entire room or structure to 135–145°F, penetrating furniture, walls, and baseboards where bed bugs hide. According to peer-reviewed studies, heat treatments achieve a 97–100% elimination rate when performed correctly. Unlike chemical treatments, bed bugs cannot develop resistance to heat. The process takes 6–8 hours depending on the size of the space, and you can return home the same day. The downside? Heat treatment is the most expensive option, typically ranging from $1,200 to $2,500 for a single-family home. But if you want guaranteed results without repeat visits, heat is unmatched. For severe infestations or multi-unit properties, this is the method professionals trust.

How Chemical Treatments Work—and Why They Require Multiple Visits

Chemical treatments use EPA-registered insecticides applied to baseboards, bed frames, mattress seams, and other harborage areas. These products work through contact or ingestion, and modern formulations include pyrethroids, neonicotinoids, and desiccants like diatomaceous earth. Chemical treatments are effective, but they require precision and patience. Bed bug eggs are resistant to most insecticides, so a second treatment is necessary 10–14 days later to kill newly hatched nymphs. Most infestations require 2–3 treatments spaced two weeks apart. Success rates hover around 70–90% depending on the severity of the infestation and the thoroughness of the application. Chemical treatments cost less upfront—usually $300 to $800 for an initial visit—but total costs add up with follow-up visits. This method works well for light to moderate infestations, especially when combined with prep work like washing linens and vacuuming. If you're looking for a lower-cost option and can tolerate a longer timeline, professional chemical treatment through a licensed provider like Shaw's Pest Control is a proven approach.

Steam and DIY Methods: When They Help and When They Fall Short

Steam treatment uses high-temperature vapor (160–180°F) applied directly to surfaces where bed bugs hide. It's effective on contact and can kill eggs, but it only works where the steam reaches. Professionals use commercial steamers with precise temperature control, but even then, steam is best used as a supplemental tool—not a standalone solution. Homeowners often use handheld steamers on mattresses and couches, which can reduce populations but rarely eliminates an infestation entirely. DIY methods like vacuuming, encasements, and diatomaceous earth play a role in integrated pest management but are not cures. Mattress encasements trap bed bugs inside and prevent new ones from entering, but they don't kill existing bugs hiding in baseboards or outlets. Diatomaceous earth is a desiccant that damages the exoskeleton, but it works slowly and only if bed bugs walk through it. Vacuuming removes visible bugs but misses eggs and hidden adults. If you're dealing with a confirmed infestation, DIY efforts alone will not solve the problem. They can, however, reduce populations and support professional treatments. For complete elimination, you need a method that reaches every hiding spot—and that's where professional bed bug control in Wichita makes the difference.

Bed Bug Treatment in Wichita: What Local Homeowners Should Know

Bed bugs don't discriminate—they've been found in apartments, hotels, single-family homes, and senior living facilities across Wichita. Kansas State University Extension notes that bed bug complaints have increased across the state over the past decade, mirroring national trends. Local pest control providers familiar with Wichita's housing stock—older homes with plaster walls, multi-family units near downtown, and newer developments in west Wichita—understand the unique challenges of treating different structures. Older homes may require more attention to cracks and voids, while apartments need coordination between units to prevent re-infestation. The key is working with a licensed, experienced provider who tailors the treatment to your specific situation. Shaw's Pest Control has served Wichita and surrounding communities since 1987, and we've seen how quickly bed bugs spread when not treated properly. If you live in Derby, Andover, or El Dorado, the same principles apply: act fast, choose a proven method, and don't rely on DIY shortcuts.

Frequently Asked Questions

What kills bed bugs instantly?

Heat above 122°F kills bed bugs on contact within minutes. Professional heat treatments and direct steam application (160°F+) are the only methods that instantly kill all life stages, including eggs. Chemical sprays kill adults on contact but do not kill eggs, which is why repeat treatments are necessary.

Can bed bugs be eliminated in one treatment?

Yes, but only with heat treatment. Whole-room or whole-structure heat treatments can eliminate an infestation in one 6–8 hour session with a 97–100% success rate. Chemical treatments require 2–3 applications spaced 10–14 days apart because insecticides don't kill eggs effectively.

How much does the best bed bug treatment cost?

Heat treatment costs $1,200–$2,500 for a typical home. Chemical treatments start at $300–$800 for the first visit, with follow-ups adding $200–$400 each. Total costs for chemical treatments often reach $800–$1,500 depending on severity. Heat is more expensive upfront but eliminates the need for return visits.

Is heat or chemical treatment better for bed bugs?

Heat treatment is more effective and faster, eliminating infestations in one visit with near-perfect success rates. Chemical treatment is less expensive initially and works well for lighter infestations, but requires multiple visits. If budget allows, heat is the best bed bug treatment for guaranteed results.

Do I need to throw away my mattress if I have bed bugs?

No. Bed bugs live in many places beyond mattresses—baseboards, outlets, furniture, and clutter. A professional treatment addresses the entire room. Use a certified bed bug mattress encasement to trap any bugs inside, and treat the room with heat or chemicals. Throwing away furniture often spreads the infestation.

How do I know if a bed bug treatment worked?

Monitor for 3–4 weeks after treatment. Look for new bites, live bugs, or dark fecal spots on sheets and baseboards. Heat treatments show results immediately. Chemical treatments require follow-up inspections 10–14 days later to confirm newly hatched nymphs are eliminated. Professional providers offer re-treatment guarantees if live bugs reappear.
